title: SafeDiSTL: Decomposing Joint Constraints for Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
title_zh: SafeDiSTL：分解联合约束以实现安全的多智能体强化学习

paragraphs.en: Cooperative multi-agent tasks often impose constraints on a shared objective or collective safety. A team level violation cost function can measure this constraint outcome, but does not distinguish which agents’ actions most strongly influence that violation. We present SafeDiSTL, a constrained multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that allows for credit assignment even with joint constraint measurements. We use Signal Temporal Logic (STL) robustness to measure episode-level violation through running-maximum cost increments. Smooth full-episode robustness and differentiable dynamics provide action sensitivities, which allocate each cost increment across agents at the same decision time. These sensitivities account for delayed effects when weighting agents’ shares of each cost increment. We study the framework in cooperative payload transport, connected navigation, and networked traffic control tasks. SafeDiSTL achieves 1.6-5.1x the safe-success rate in transport, improves navigation safe-success by 11.1%, and delivers 50-68% more throughput in traffic when compared to constrained baselines. Results demonstrate a strong improvement of the learned policy in dealing with shared constraint while retaining the performance of unconstrained policies.
paragraphs.zh: 协作式多智能体任务通常会对共享目标或集体安全施加约束。 团队层面的违规成本函数可以衡量这种约束结果，但无法区分哪些智能体的行为对该违规的影响最大。 我们提出了 SafeDiSTL，一种受约束的多智能体强化学习框架，该框架即使在联合测量约束的情况下也能实现责任分配。 我们通过运行最大值成本的增量，利用信号时域逻辑（STL）的鲁棒性来衡量单轮任务中的违规程度。 平滑的全轮任务鲁棒性和可微分的动态特性提供了行为敏感度，从而在相同决策时刻将每个成本增量分配给各智能体。 这些敏感度在计算各智能体对每个成本增量的贡献时，会考虑延迟效应的影响。 我们在协作式有效载荷运输、连接导航和网络化交通控制任务中对该框架进行了研究。 与受约束的基线方法相比，SafeDiSTL 在运输任务中的安全成功率提升了 1.6-5.1 倍，导航任务的安全成功率提高了 11.1%，交通任务的吞吐量则提升了 50-68%。 实验结果表明，所学习策略在应对共享约束方面显著改进，同时仍保留了无约束策略的性能水平。

paragraphs.en: Recent developments in multi-agent autonomous systems and their applications in aerial swarms, intelligent transportation networks, and automated warehouses have made multi-agent coordination a central problem. In these environments, multiple agents must operate in shared spaces and achieve collective objectives, including collaborative manipulation, routing, and formation control, while satisfying system constraints such as connectivity and collision avoidance. Constraints in single-agent RL are commonly formulated with Constrained Markov Decision Processes (CMDPs) [ 2 ] . Policies are then optimized by reformulating the problem as a primal-dual optimization between reward and costs. Constrained Policy Optimization (CPO) [ 1 ] balances updates with more reward or cost consideration using a Lagrangian multiplier. Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) is a popular paradigm for learning decentralized agent policies in multi-agent problems. Existing work extends CMDP formulations to MARL [ 11 ] , although generally assuming well-defined, decoupled cost functions for individual agents. However, a shared constraint definition is important in multi-agent settings. For example, if multiple robots carry a shared rigid payload, a crash between the payload and obstacles is hard to attribute to individual agents. Consider the example shown in Figure 1 : three warehouse robots collaboratively transport a large payload to a designated delivery location. At a given point t 3 t_{3} , one robot might be required to push in a direction such that the payload avoids the obstacle (green agent pushing up), while the other two maintain progress toward the goal (yellow and blue push right). When encountering a violation such as that in Figure 1 .(a), assigning equal responsibility to all agents leads to a deadlock (Figure 1 .(b)) without addressing the asymmetrical desired updates to individual agents. This shows that a shared constraint definition alone is not enough. It tells the team of agents how much they violated, but without explicit learning signals to individual agents on how to update their policies. Without careful decomposition, the introduction of a uniform penalty for all agents will hinder task learning progress. If an agent makes significant contribution towards the team’s task progress but not towards violating constraint at a timestep, that individual transition should not incur a penalty in the policy learning process.

paragraphs.en: Credit assignment is an active area of research in MARL. Counterfactual Multi-Agent Policy Gradients (COMA) [ 9 ] established counterfactual reasoning for agents on task reward. Existing work [ 11 , 17 , 14 ] considers both individual and shared constraints in MARL problems, but leaves much to be desired in the effective decomposition of the constraint objective. This motivates the need for a principled mechanism to decompose the shared constraint among agents while accounting for the changing individual responsibilities to enable effective collaboration. Signal Temporal Logic (STL) [ 16 ] is a compact formal specification language that expresses logical and temporal requirements over trajectories. The quantitative measure called robustness [ 7 , 8 ] assigns the margin of success to a trajectory instead of a binary signal. The biggest advantage of using STL is that differentiating its robustness through the full trajectory captures how individual actions influence subsequent constraint outcomes. We use these gradients to allocate cost increments across agents at its original timestep, while cost advantages propagate learning signals to earlier decisions. For the example in Figure 1 , we express the shared responsibility as "Always no collision between payload and obstacle". Differentiable dynamics help achieve this by propagating individual agents’ influence to joint state space trajectories, and allowing back propagation from the margin of violation to decisions. As shown in Figure 1 .(c), the green agent learns to subtly change its behavior by pushing upward rather than to the right, resulting in a successful avoidance of the obstacle. paragraphs.en: We introduce an agent- and time-specific attribution mechanism that decomposes shared team constraints using STL robustness gradients while preserving the total cost.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了一种针对特定智能体和时间的归因机制，该机制利用 STL 鲁棒性梯度分解共享的团队约束，同时保持总成本不变。

paragraphs.en: We develop SafeDiSTL, a constrained MARL framework that incorporates these attributed costs into policy optimization for decentralized execution.

paragraphs.en: We evaluate SafeDiSTL on three tasks, comparing task performance and constraint satisfaction with other baselines.

paragraphs.en: Constrained MARL: Gu et al. [ 11 ] introduce MACPO and MAPPO-Lagrangian, using constrained trust region updates and Lagrangian policy optimization, respectively. Like MACPO, IsCPO [ 17 ] coordinates separate agent policies through sequential updates. IsCPO considers global costs and updates agents in random order, passing optimization information to subsequent agents. Thus, later agents account for the effects of earlier updates on the shared constraint. Both MACPO and IsCPO coordinate policy updates, rather than an explicit allocation of a trajectory’s violation cost according to each agent’s influence. Ling et al. [ 14 ] directly address constraint credit assignment through fictitious MARL in a collective setting. Its formulation exploits anonymous interactions represented by aggregate counts of agents in local states and actions, rather than individual identities. This structure supports scalable reward and constraint credit assignment, but is not assumed in our setting, where shared constraints can depend on coupled geometric configurations and action-dependent dynamics. SafeDiSTL instead obtains agent-specific cost allocations from the gradient sensitivity of a shared trajectory specification.
paragraphs.zh: 受约束 MARL：Gu 等人 [ 11 ] 提出了 MACPO 和 MAPPO-Lagrangian，分别采用了受约束的信任区域更新和拉格朗日策略优化。 与 MACPO 类似，IsCPO [ 17 ] 通过顺序更新来协调各个智能体的策略。 IsCPO 会考虑全局成本，并以随机顺序更新智能体，同时将优化信息传递给后续的智能体。 因此，后续的智能体会将早期更新对共享约束的影响纳入考量。 MACPO 和 IsCPO 都通过协调策略更新来实现协作，而不是根据每个智能体的影响对轨迹的违规成本进行显式分配。Ling 等人 [ 14 ] 通过在集体环境中使用虚拟 MARL，直接解决了约束信用分配问题。 其公式利用了匿名交互，这种交互由局部状态和行动中智能体的汇总数量表示，而非个体身份。 这种结构支持可扩展的奖励和约束信用分配，但在我们的设定中并未假设这一点，因为共享约束可能依赖于耦合的几何构型以及依赖行动的动力学特性。 SafeDiSTL 则通过共享轨迹规格的梯度敏感性来获取针对每个智能体的特定成本分配。

sents.en: Its formulation exploits anonymous interactions represented by aggregate counts of agents in local states and actions, rather than individual identities.

sents.en: This structure supports scalable reward and constraint credit assignment, but is not assumed in our setting, where shared constraints can depend on coupled geometric configurations and action-dependent dynamics.

sents.en: SafeDiSTL instead obtains agent-specific cost allocations from the gradient sensitivity of a shared trajectory specification.

paragraphs.en: Multi-agent Credit Assignment: Credit assignment methods for multi-agent systems extract individual learning signals from shared team outcomes. COMA [ 9 ] uses a centralized critic and a counterfactual baseline that marginalizes one agent’s action while holding the others fixed. QPD [ 21 ] applies integrated gradients along trajectory paths to decompose global action values into individual credits. STAS [ 5 ] first redistributes episodic return over time and then uses Shapley attribution between agents. These methods establish counterfactual, gradient-based, and temporal attribution for cooperative reward optimization. Our focus is the attribution of the shared constraint: we differentiate STL robustness through dynamics rather than attribute a learned return prediction.
paragraphs.zh: 多智能体信用分配：多智能体系统的信用分配方法能够从共享的团队结果中提取个体的学习信号。 COMA [ 9 ] 使用一个集中式评论器和一个反事实基线，该基线在保持其他智能体动作不变的同时，对单个智能体的动作进行边缘化处理。 QPD [ 21 ] 沿着轨迹路径应用集成梯度，将全局动作值分解为个体信用。 STAS [ 5 ] 首先将回合制回报在时间上重新分配，然后在智能体之间使用沙普利归因方法。 这些方法为合作性奖励优化建立了反事实、基于梯度和时间维度的归因机制。 我们的重点是共享约束的归因：我们通过动态过程来区分 STL 鲁棒性，而不是对已学习的回报预测进行归因。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate SafeDiSTL on three cooperative multi-agent benchmarks with different shared constraints: package–obstacle clearance in transport, communication connectivity in navigation, and core occupancy in traffic control. Across tasks, we examine whether attribution of a shared constraint supports task completion while maintaining constraint satisfaction. We compare against reward-only MAPPO and the constrained baselines MACPO and MAPPO-L from Gu et. al. [ 11 ] . Baseline optimization details are provided in Appendix A .
paragraphs.zh: 我们在三个具有不同共享约束的合作多智能体基准测试上评估了 SafeDiSTL：运输中的包裹与障碍物避让、导航中的通信连通性，以及交通控制中的核心区域占用。 我们跨多个任务检验了共享约束的归因是否能在维持约束满足的同时支持任务完成。 我们将它与仅使用奖励的 MAPPO，以及 Gu 等人 [11] 提出的受约束基线方法 MACPO 和 MAPPO-L 进行了比较。 基线方法的优化细节见附录 A。

paragraphs.en: All methods use six training seeds and common evaluation resets within each benchmark. We compare task success, shared constraint satisfaction, and their joint occurrence, as well as task returns. All methods are trained with the same compute budget in each scenario in terms of simulation steps. Transport policies train with 15M sim steps, and evaluates on 500 common resets per obstacle condition. Navigation policie train with 15M sim steps, and evaluates on 128 common resets. Traffic policies train with 20M sim steps and evaluates on 1,000 common resets. In all benchmarks, SafeDiSTL uses the running max increment cost defined in Secion 5.1 . All other benchmarks utilizes cost functions equivalent to the per step cost of the same STL specification. For example, in transport, SafeDiSTL’s STL specification says "Always no collision between the payload and the obstacles", the equivalent per step cost function is the overlapping margin in Euclidean distance between the payload and obstacles’ geometric shapes. Each method then pre-processes the cost functions according to the reference implementation. All experiments are conducted in JAX [ 4 ] on GPUs. We primarily examine four key metrics.
paragraphs.zh: 所有方法均使用六个训练种子，并在每个基准测试中采用共同的评估重置。 我们比较任务成功、共享约束满足及其共同出现的情况，以及任务回报。 在所有场景中，所有方法均以相同的计算预算（以模拟步数衡量）进行训练。 运输策略使用 1500 万模拟步数进行训练，并在每种障碍物条件下基于 500 次共同重置进行评估。 导航策略使用 1500 万模拟步数进行训练，并在 128 次共同重置上进行评估。 交通策略使用 2000 万模拟步数进行训练，并在 1000 次共同重置上进行评估。 在所有基准测试中，SafeDiSTL 均使用第 5.1 节中定义的运行最大增量成本。 所有其他基准测试均使用与相同 STL 规范每一步成本等效的成本函数。 例如，在运输任务中，SafeDiSTL 的 STL 规范规定“货物与障碍物之间始终无碰撞”，其等效的每一步成本函数是货物与障碍物几何形状之间欧几里得距离上的重叠余量。 随后，每种方法都根据参考实现对成本函数进行预处理。 所有实验均在 JAX [4] 上通过 GPU 执行。 我们主要考察四个关键指标。

paragraphs.en: We first show the key result of the experiments. In Figure 2 , we show that SafeDiSTL balances the tradeoff between constraint satisfaction and retaining performance. In each subplot, the y y -axes shows constraint satisfaction metrics in percentages, and the x x -axes shows performance metrics in normalized returns to those obtained by MAPPO. Our algorithm modifies MAPPO by introducing the dual on constraint and asymmetric cost attribution to individual agents, thus we want to show that SafeDiSTL retains the performance of MAPPO, but does so considering satisfying the shared constraints. In all five scenarios shown in Figure 2 , SafeDiSTL balances this trade off by being in the top right quadrant of the plots, while other methods sacrifice MAPPO’s task performance to increase constraint satisfaction. Appendix E examines attribution, cost formulation, and dual-optimizer variants.
paragraphs.zh: 我们首先展示实验的关键结果。 在图 2 中，我们展示了 SafeDiSTL 如何在满足约束与保留性能之间取得平衡。 在每个子图中，y 轴以百分比形式显示约束满足度指标，而 x 轴则以相对于 MAPPO 所得结果的归一化回报形式显示性能指标。 我们的算法通过引入对约束的对偶处理以及将成本非对称地分配给各个智能体来改进 MAPPO，因此我们希望证明 SafeDiSTL 能够保留 MAPPO 的性能，同时考虑满足共享的约束条件。 在图 2 所示的全部五个场景中，SafeDiSTL 通过位于图表的右上角象限实现了这一平衡，而其他方法则牺牲了 MAPPO 的任务性能以提高约束满足度。 附录 E 探讨了成本归因、成本构建以及对偶优化器变体。

paragraphs.en: We use a transport task with dynamics and control similar to the one in [ 3 ] , where three force input agents push a shared package around circular obstacles towards a goal. The shared constraint here is package–obstacle clearance, and safe success requires both the payload reaching the goal and no contact between the payload and the obstacle throughout the entire episode. In this benchmark, we consider three different settings with 1-3 obstacles between the starting position and the payload goal. Figure 3 shows the comparison between the four methods. SafeDiSTL has the highest mean safe success rate in all three settings: 35.6 ± 9.6 % 35.6\pm 9.6\% , 16.2 ± 11.0 % 16.2\pm 11.0\% , and 3.5 ± 2.3 % 3.5\pm 2.3\% with one, two, and three obstacles, respectively. MAPPO-L trails closest behind with 7.0 ± 3.7 % 7.0\pm 3.7\% , 4.5 ± 0.9 % 4.5\pm 0.9\% , and 2.2 ± 1.0 % 2.2\pm 1.0\% . With three obstacles, safe success remains low for all methods in this harder condition, yet SafeDiSTL still achieves highest safe success rate there. Although MAPPO has higher mean goal success in all three conditions, SafeDiSTL more often achieves the goal while satisfying the shared clearance requirement. MACPO on the other hand completely fails in all three settings. Full numerical results appear in Table 1 . Figure 4 shows an example rollout comparison between the methods. The same trend shows up here as well: MAPPO reaches the goal, the two constrained baselines has degraded goal reaching capability, while SafeDiSTL manages to go around the obstacle and reaches the goal.

paragraphs.en: In this benchmark, we control four point-mass agents navigating through two staggered obstacle passages to a shared destination. The shared constraint is buffered full episode communication connectivity: at every timestep, the longest edge of the agents’ Euclidean minimum-spanning tree must not exceed 3.325 3.325 m. Goal success requires all agents to remain in the destination region during the final 20 control steps. Figure 6 reports the comparison between all four methods. SafeDiSTL has the highest mean goal success rate ( 71.88 ± 6.13 % 71.88\pm 6.13\% ) and safe-success rate ( 43.88 ± 4.40 % 43.88\pm 4.40\% ) among the four main methods. MAPPO-L attains slightly higher full episode constraint satisfaction rate than SafeDiSTL ( 56.64 ± 10.61 % 56.64\pm 10.61\% versus 54.69 ± 8.33 % 54.69\pm 8.33\% ). MACPO reaches only 4.43 ± 1.96 % 4.43\pm 1.96\% safe successes. MAPPO has the highest mean return but almost always violates the constraint. These results show that in the connected navigation benchmark, considering the constraint effectively also helps with task success rate since grouping together through the narrow passage reduces accidental collision with the obstacle that might slow down goal reaching. Full numerical results appear in Table 2 . Figure 5 also shows the same conclusion in matched rollout trajectories. SafeDiSTL agents grouped closely together and navigated smoothly towards the goal without any disconnects in the graph. The agents in all other methods disconnected at least once throughout the episode.

paragraphs.en: We consider a seven region Networked Macroscopic Fundamental Diagram (NMFD) traffic task [ 10 , 19 ] . Six peripheral regions exchange destination labeled traffic through a shared central core. Each region meters its outgoing traffic, while core exits are uncontrolled and randomized at every time step. The shared constraint is on the core region’s occupancy. The flow rate of the core region is dictated by the cubic polynomial shown in Figure 7 . The flow rate first increases as the number of vehicles in the region increases. After the peak, it drops down to the congestion limit, where the flow rate drops below 1 vehicle per second. Thus the shared constraint is set as n core ≤ n safe ≃ 8786.415 n_{\mathrm{core}}\leq n_{\mathrm{safe}}\simeq 8786.415 . Vehicle admissions to the core therefore trade off completed trips against core region congestion, while restrictive metering can increase the wait time in the system.
paragraphs.zh: 我们考虑一个包含七个区域的网络宏观基础图（NMFD）交通任务 [ 10 , 19 ] 。 六个外围区域通过一个共享的核心区域交换带有目的地标签的交通流。 每个区域都会测量其出向交通流量，而核心区域的出口在每个时间步都是不受控制且随机化的。 共享的约束条件针对的是核心区域的占用率。 核心区域的流量速率由图 7 中所示的三次多项式决定。 随着区域内车辆数量的增加，流量速率首先会上升。 达到峰值后，流量速率会下降至拥堵极限，此时流量速率降至每秒 1 辆车以下。 因此，共享约束条件设定为 n core ≤ n safe ≃ 8786.415 n_{\mathrm{core}}\leq n_{\mathrm{safe}}\simeq 8786.415 。 因此，车辆进入核心区域需要在已完成行程与核心区域拥堵之间进行权衡，而严格的流量控制可能会增加系统中的等待时间。

All vehicles must travel through the core on their way to their destinations. The agents control their own regions’ flow rate for vehicles with all other peripheral regions as destination. Then the system revolves following the controlled core region in-flow rate, and the uncontrolled, randomized out-flow rate. The agents observe the randomize exit rate, and should react to changes for decisions on their control. For this task, since there isn’t a clear measure for success, we use these key metrics instead:

paragraphs.en: Completed trips: this is the equivalent to task return, where the policy uses as training reward.
paragraphs.zh: 已完成行程：这与任务回报相当，策略会将其用作训练奖励。

paragraphs.en: Overload-free episode rate: the percentage of full episodes without overloading the core region.
paragraphs.zh: 无过载回合率：完整回合中未对核心区域造成过载的百分比。

paragraphs.en: Core vehicle-hours: the time that vehicles spends on average at the core region, this measures the system delay.
paragraphs.zh: 核心车辆小时数：车辆在核心区域平均花费的时间，该指标用于衡量系统延迟。

paragraphs.en: Time above core limit: the time that core regions has occupancy higher than the limit.
paragraphs.zh: 核心区域超限时间：核心区域的占用率高于限制值的时间。

paragraphs.en: Figure 8 compares all four methods. The training reward for all methods here are completed trips. The goal of this benchmark is to test the trade off between throughput and core congestion. Since core region exit rates are randomized, a smart team of agents should learn to coordinate when to let each destination’s vehicles go without overloading the core. SafeDiSTL retains 71.4 % 71.4\% of MAPPO throughput while reducing the core vehicle-hours to 8.8 % 8.8\% of MAPPO and the time above core limits to 0.3 % 0.3\% of MAPPO. Although MACPO and MAPPO-L also learn to reduce constraint violation to the same level, they only retain 47.6 % 47.6\% and 42.5 % 42.5\% of the MAPPO throughput, respectively. paragraphs.en: We propose SafeDiSTL, a constrained MARL framework that allows for credit assignment under shared team constraints. Using STL robustness gradients, we derive a cost attribution scheme that decomposes the shared team constraints while preserving the total cost. These attributed costs are then incorporated in policy optimization for centralized training and decentralized execution. Across three diverse case studies on cooperative payload transport, connected navigation, and traffic network control, SafeDiSTL shows a strong improvement in handling shared constraints over the other state-of-the art MARL baselines.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 SafeDiSTL，这是一种受约束的多智能体强化学习（MARL）框架，能够在共享团队约束条件下进行功劳分配。 通过利用 STL 鲁棒性梯度，我们推导出了一种成本归因方案，该方案在保持总成本不变的同时，将共享团队约束进行了分解。 随后，这些归因后的成本被整合到策略优化中，用于集中式训练和去中心化执行。 在合作货物运输、连接导航和交通网络控制这三个不同领域的案例研究中，SafeDiSTL 在处理共享约束方面的表现显著优于其他当前最先进的 MARL 基线方法。

paragraphs.en: First, while SafeDiSTL has shown an exceptional safety performance tradeoff in benchmarks, it relies on the gradients of the robustness signal through the system dynamics. The dynamics gradients might be hard to come by in contact-rich scenarios. Even with non-differentiable dynamics, we can still estimate via finite differences by using more calls to the simulation. Future extensions should aim to mitigate this issue by devising gradient-free signals for STL robustness decomposition. Second, our sensitivity metric used to allocate costs is the magnitude of influence. Future work could also consider how to incorporate the direction of influence. Third, we did not show benchmarks on higher fidelity robotic scenarios, and potential transfer of learned policies to real robots. Future works will include validation of the proposed method on real-world robotic platforms.
paragraphs.zh: 首先，尽管 SafeDiSTL 在基准测试中展现了卓越的安全性能权衡，但它依赖于通过系统动态传递的鲁棒性信号的梯度。 在接触频繁的场景中，获取动态梯度可能十分困难。 即使面对不可微分的动态系统，我们仍可通过增加模拟调用次数，利用有限差分法进行估计。 未来的扩展应致力于设计无需梯度的信号，以缓解 STL 鲁棒性分解中的这一问题。 其次，我们用于分配成本的敏感度指标是影响力的大小。 未来的研究还可以考虑如何将影响力的方向纳入考量。 第三，我们尚未展示更高保真度机器人场景下的基准测试，也未展示所学习策略向真实机器人的潜在迁移效果。 未来的工作将包括在真实世界的机器人平台上验证所提出的方法。

paragraphs.en: Multi-Agent Constrained Policy Optimisation (MACPO) updates decentralized actors sequentially, accounting for the policies of agents already updated in the current iteration [ 11 ] . Each actor maximizes a reward surrogate subject to cost constraints and a Kullback–Leibler (KL) trust region. Thus, coordination enters the sequential surrogate rather than a simultaneous update of all actors using a fixed cost penalty.

paragraphs.en: Four homogeneous planar agents navigate from a compact start formation to a shared circular destination through two staggered obstacle passages. The canonical corridor is 18 m long and 10 m wide; ten static circular obstacles form two five-obstacle barriers. Agent and obstacle radii are 0.75 m and 0.8 m, respectively. Resets randomize barrier locations, opening centers, and opening widths (3.4–3.8 m), perturb the start formation and destination, and apply a global rotation, reflection, and translation. Agents use bounded two-dimensional acceleration commands, maximum speed 1.5 m/s, smooth contact forces, five physics substeps per 0.1 s control step, and a 250-step horizon. The shared reward combines reduction in mean agent-to-goal distance, scaled by 5 / R 5/R , with the fraction of agents inside the destination. Goal success requires all four agents to remain within the 2.6 m goal radius throughout the final 20 control steps.

paragraphs.en: This section describes the actor inputs and policy networks used in the reported benchmarks.

paragraphs.en: For agent i i , the observation concatenates its absolute planar position and velocity (four coordinates), package position minus goal position (two), package position relative to the agent (two), absolute package velocity (two), and a binary package-on-goal indicator (one). It then includes the relative position of each of the K K obstacles ( 2 ​ K 2K coordinates) and the relative position and velocity of each of the other two agents (eight coordinates), ordered by agent index. Thus the observation dimension is 19 + 2 ​ K 19+2K , giving 21, 23, and 25 inputs for the one-, two-, and three-obstacle conditions. The nonrotating package contributes no orientation features, and no assigned push-slot features are appended. Actor inputs are standardized using running means and variances estimated during training and clipped to [ − 10 , 10 ] [-10,10] ; evaluation uses the saved normalization statistics without updating them.

paragraphs.en: The actor is a feed-forward multilayer perceptron with two 64-unit hidden layers, tanh activations, and a linear two-dimensional Gaussian-mean head. Training samples a latent Gaussian action and applies tanh to obtain the normalized force command in [ − 1 , 1 ] 2 [-1,1]^{2} ; deterministic evaluation applies tanh to the mean. The simulator multiplies this command by 0.6. MAPPO, SafeDiSTL, and the uniform-attribution variants share one actor across the three agents; MAPPO-L and MACPO use separate actor parameters for each agent with the same layer sizes and action parameterization.

paragraphs.en: Each agent receives a 72-dimensional observation. The first 34 coordinates comprise its own planar position and velocity (four), normalized episode time (one), four relative target positions (eight), and three teammate slots (21). The four target entries refer to the shared destination. Each teammate slot contains relative position and velocity from the stored communication packet, a direct-neighbor indicator, a connected-component reachability indicator, and packet age; slots follow the agents’ fixed identifiers within the episode. The remaining 38 coordinates describe the ten obstacles using relative position and radius (30), the four corridor-boundary clearances (four), and the flattened two-dimensional world-rotation matrix (four). Positions, relative distances, obstacle radii, and boundary clearances are divided by 10; velocities are divided by the maximum speed of 1.5; time and packet ages are divided by the 250-step horizon. These features are then standardized using running observation statistics and clipped to [ − 10 , 10 ] [-10,10] , with the saved statistics held fixed during evaluation.
paragraphs.zh: 每个智能体接收一个 72 维的观测数据。 前 34 个坐标包括其自身的平面位置和速度（4）、归一化的回合时间（1）、四个相对目标位置（8）以及三个队友槽位（21）。 四个目标条目指的是共享的目的地。 每个队友槽位包含来自已存储通信包的相对位置和速度、直接邻居指示器、连通组件可达性指示器以及数据包年龄；槽位按照回合内智能体的固定标识符排列。 其余 38 个坐标用于描述十个障碍物，包括相对位置和半径（30）、四个走廊边界距离（4）以及扁平化的二维世界旋转矩阵（4）。 位置、相对距离、障碍物半径和边界距离均除以 10；速度除以最大速度 1.5；时间和数据包年龄则除以 250 步的时间范围。 随后，这些特征使用运行时的观测统计数据进行标准化，并裁剪至 [−10, 10]，在评估过程中保存的统计数据保持固定不变。

paragraphs.en: Each peripheral agent receives 31 observation coordinates: its six destination-specific queues, six local origin–destination demand rates, six destination-specific queues in the shared core, six current effective core-exit factors, normalized episode time, and a six-dimensional one-hot agent identity. paragraphs.en: The actor has two 64-unit tanh hidden layers and a linear six-dimensional Gaussian-mean head, with a learned, observation-independent log-standard-deviation vector. A sigmoid transforms each latent Gaussian sample into an admission command in [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] . The self-destination coordinate is masked to zero, leaving five effective controls per agent; deterministic evaluation applies the same sigmoid and mask to the mean. MAPPO, SafeDiSTL, and the uniform-attribution variants share one actor across the six agents. MAPPO-L and MACPO instead maintain six independent actors with the same input features, hidden-layer sizes, and action transform.
paragraphs.zh: 该智能体包含两个 64 个单元的双曲正切（tanh）隐藏层和一个线性六维高斯均值头，并配有一个经过学习、与观察无关的对数标准差向量。一个 Sigmoid 函数将每个潜在的高斯样本转换为 [0,1] 范围内的准入指令。自目标坐标被掩码为零，因此每个智能体只剩下五个有效控制项；确定性评估则对均值应用相同的 Sigmoid 函数和掩码。MAPPO、SafeDiSTL 以及均匀归因变体在六个智能体之间共享一个智能体。而 MAPPO-L 和 MACPO 则维持六个独立的智能体，其输入特征、隐藏层大小和行动转换均相同。
